therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: Adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus inadequately controlled on metformin
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: Change from baseline in HbA1c at weeks 26 and 52

results.effect_size: LS mean difference -0.47% at week 26; -0.42% at week 52
results.target_engagement_evidence: Reduction in proinsulin/insulin ratio (LS mean difference -0.041, p<0.001) and improvement in HOMA beta-cell function (LS mean difference +12.963%, p<0.001) consistent with DPP-4 inhibition and incretin effect
biomarker_changes: HbA1c reduced by -0.89% (alogliptin+pioglitazone+metformin) vs -0.42% (pioglitazone+metformin) at week 26
Fasting plasma glucose LS mean difference -10.9 mg/dL at week 26 (p<0.001)
HOMA beta-cell function LS mean difference +12.963% (p<0.001)
Apolipoprotein C-III LS mean difference -0.5 mg/dL (p=0.022)
Adiponectin LS mean difference -2.92 µg/mL (p<0.001) favoring pioglitazone 45 mg arm
HOMA insulin resistance not significantly different (p=0.567)
Body weight increase numerically less in alogliptin+pioglitazone arm (1.10 kg vs 1.60 kg at week 52, p=0.071)
subgroup_findings: At week 26, 72.0% vs 42.1% achieved ≥0.5% HbA1c reduction
Marked hyperglycemia (FPG ≥200 mg/dL) occurred in 27.3% vs 36.1% (p<0.001)
Hyperglycemic rescue criteria met in 10.9% vs 21.7% (p<0.001)
safety_signals: Serious cardiovascular events (MI, unstable angina, CAD) reported in both arms
Non-cardiac chest pain reported in 2 patients in alogliptin+pioglitazone+metformin arm
Cataracts reported in 2 patients in pioglitazone 45 mg arm

dose_info.dose: Alogliptin 25 mg + Pioglitazone 30 mg (combination arm); Pioglitazone 45 mg (comparator arm); Metformin ≥1500 mg or maximum tolerated dose

modulation_entries.hypothesis: DPP-4 inhibition by alogliptin raises active GLP-1/GIP levels, enhancing beta-cell insulin secretion and complementing pioglitazone's insulin-sensitizing effect to produce greater glycemic lowering than pioglitazone alone
modulation_entries.citation: LS mean difference = -0.47, alogliptin+pioglitazone+metformin vs pioglitazone+metformin at week 26; HOMA beta-cell function LS mean difference = 12.963% (p<0.001)

modulation_entries.hypothesis: Metformin suppresses hepatic glucose output, providing a complementary mechanism to pioglitazone's peripheral insulin sensitization, together improving overall glycemic control beyond either agent alone
modulation_entries.citation: Metformin ≥1500 mg or maximum tolerated dose was the background therapy in both arms, and both arms showed HbA1c reductions consistent with additive glycemic lowering
